title: College student sentenced to jail, probation for sending 16-year-old girl money for explicit images - NewsBreak
text:
By Sorina Trauntvein ,
3 hours ago
CEDAR CITY, Utah ( ABC4 ) — A University of Utah student has been sentenced to less than a year of jail time and probation for sending a 16-year-old girl money in exchange for sexually explicit images and videos.
In April, 31-year-old Sergio Yahir Cruz Fajardo was arrested and charged with 12 counts of sexual exploitation of a minor, a second-degree felony. He pleaded guilty to two of those charges on June 3, and the remaining 10 were dismissed with prejudice as part of a plea agreement.
On Wednesday, a Fifth District Court judge handed down a sentence to Cruz Fajardo. He was sentenced to two terms of 1 to 15 years at the Utah State Prison. However, those sentences were suspended.
PREVIOUSLY: University of Utah student pleads guilty to sending 16-year-old girl money for explicit images Instead, Cruz Fajardo was ordered to serve 364 days in jail with credit for 125 days of time served. He was also placed on probation for the next 48 months (four years) and ordered to register as a Group A sex offender.
If Cruz Fajardo violates the terms of his probation — including no contact with the victim, abiding by sex offender requirements, and obtaining employment — he could serve the suspended prison sentence.
Case background The charges stem from Nov. 30, 2025, when the Cedar City Police Department responded to a domestic dispute between a 16-year-old girl and her mother. When officers arrived, they learned that the fight had started after the mother learned that her daughter was speaking with an older man on Snapchat.
PAST COVERAGE: College student jailed for sending 16-year-old girl money for explicit images Police conducted a consensual search of the teen’s phone and found that the 16-year-old had distributed explicit videos and images of herself to adults in exchange for money. One of the adults went by “Carlos,” and police found Cash App transactions between him and the teen.
The 16-year-old stated that “Carlos” added her on Snapchat, and she added him back. From there, they exchanged messages for a month. At one point, the teen asked him for money, and he requested explicit images of the teen.
An officer with the Cedar City Police Department submitted several search warrants to gain more information about “Carlos.” Using the Cash App account details, he linked the account to 31-year-old Cruz Fajardo.
Additional information from Cash App showed that he tried to send the 16-year-old more money, but the app flagged it as risky or involving a minor, and they did not go through.
How to make ABC4 your preferred news source on Google Using an undercover account posing as a 15-year-old girl, the Cedar City Police officer added Cruz Fajardo on Snapchat. During their conversations, Cruz Fajardo allegedly admitted to being a current student at the University of Utah.
Documents say that the University of Utah Police Department confirmed that Cruz Fajardo attended the university and lived nearby in Salt Lake City.
On April 2, Cruz Fajardo was arrested by the Salt Lake City Police Department and later transferred and booked into the Iron County Jail.
